reason: The text depicts Moses and Aaron (the Hebrew leaders) negotiating with Pharaoh on behalf of the Hebrew people (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), saying 'Let my people go, and they shall serve me' (שַׁלַּח עַמִּי וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי). The miracles/plagues are directed against Egypt to force Pharaoh's compliance and secure the liberation of Israel from bondage. Notably, the text explicitly states that during the plague of darkness, 'for all the children of Israel there was light in their dwellings' (וּֽלְכָל־ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָם), demonstrating that the leaders are protecting and advocating for the people, not opposing them. The leaders are demonstrably supportive and liberatory toward the Hebrew people.
